validation_question: Can the board compile, upload, and resume Blink after reset?
observed_result: Arduino IDE 2.3.10; Arduino Uno; COM4; Blink compiled and uploaded; the onboard LED resumed regular blinking after reset.
notes: Board-only validation; no servo was connected.

validation_question: Does the adapter-to-breadboard path provide the intended polarity and approximately nominal 5 V?
observed_result: Adapter polarity, barrel-terminal polarity, breadboard-rail continuity, and rail voltage were checked; all were normal. The exact no-load voltage was not recorded.
notes: The multimeter check was completed before the servo was connected.

validation_question: Does S17-SERVO-A move repeatedly within a narrow commanded-angle range without reset or persistent buzzing?
observed_result: The SG90 moved between 80 and 100 deg for five cycles and returned to 90 deg. No board reset, USB disconnect, persistent buzzing, or obvious abnormal heating or smell was observed.
notes: The board was powered by USB; the servo was powered by the external 5 V rail; common ground was used.

validation_question: Does the assembled gripper move manually without clear mechanical interference before powered testing?
observed_result: The gripper was assembled and manually opened and closed. No clear mid-range mechanical interference or acrylic damage was observed.
notes: The servo horn was aligned after commanding the servo to 90 deg.

validation_question: What commanded-angle range provides sufficient opening and closing without observed interference or persistent buzzing?
observed_result: Angle increase opened the gripper and angle decrease closed it. The tested 60-120 deg range operated without observed mechanical interference or persistent buzzing. Selected endpoints were CLOSE 60 deg, OPEN 120 deg, and startup 90 deg.
notes: Physical shaft angle was not independently measured. An object-retention test was not performed.

validation_question: Do incremental OPEN and CLOSE commands, STOP, direction reversal, duplicate-state handling, and endpoint clamping operate as intended?
observed_result: OPEN, CLOSE, STOP, direction reversal, duplicate OPEN handling, and endpoint clamping were observed in the Arduino internal test sequence. No sustained instability, gear skip, or out-of-range motion was observed.
notes: STOP means no further commanded-angle updates; it is not an emergency stop or torque release.

validation_question: Does startup or reset avoid unsafe endpoint motion and recover to the configured startup behavior?
observed_result: A brief repeatable initial displacement was observed. It did not develop into sustained oscillation, unsafe endpoint excursion, persistent stall or buzzing, or board reset.
notes: The cause was not isolated; servo initialization and mechanical play are possible contributors.

validation_question: Was the final configuration reproduced beyond a single trial without a major observed failure?
observed_result: The configuration was operated repeatedly during endpoint calibration and actuator-state testing. No board reset, persistent stall or buzzing, gear skip, or out-of-range motion was observed. A separately counted 10-cycle protocol was not performed.
notes: Do not report this as a formal 10-cycle or 30-cycle reliability test.
